fr: La mairie est fermée le dimanche.
en: The town hall is closed on Sundays.
ipa: /la mɛ.ʁi ɛ fɛʁ.me lə di.mɑ̃ʃ/
notes: Feminine agreement adds a silent -e to 'fermée' that you cannot hear, only see.

fr: Les enfants jouent dans le parc.
en: The children play in the park.
ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʒu dɑ̃ lə paʁk/
notes: Liaison joins 'les' and 'enfants' with a z sound: les-z-enfants.

fr: Nous habitons dans un grand immeuble.
en: We live in a big apartment building.
ipa: /nuz‿a.bi.tɔ̃ dɑ̃z‿œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃t‿i.mœbl/
notes: Both 'nous habitons' and 'un grand immeuble' need liaison consonants you must supply in writing.

fr: La bibliothèque ouvre à neuf heures.
en: The library opens at nine o'clock.
ipa: /la bi.bli.jɔ.tɛk uvʁ a nœv‿œʁ/
notes: The liaison in 'neuf heures' makes the f sound like a v.

fr: Les voitures roulent trop vite dans cette rue.
en: The cars drive too fast on this street.
ipa: /le vwa.tyʁ ʁul tʁo vit dɑ̃ sɛt ʁy/
notes: The verb ending '-ent' in 'roulent' is never pronounced.

fr: Le bus arrive dans dix minutes.
en: The bus arrives in ten minutes.
ipa: /lə bys a.ʁiv dɑ̃ di mi.nyt/
notes: Unlike most French words, the final s in 'bus' is pronounced.

fr: Elle traverse la rue avec prudence.
en: She crosses the street carefully.
ipa: /ɛl tʁa.vɛʁs la ʁy a.vɛk pʁy.dɑ̃s/
notes: The ending '-ence' in 'prudence' carries a nasal sound, easy to misspell as '-ance'.

fr: Les rues sont très animées le soir.
en: The streets are very lively in the evening.
ipa: /le ʁy sɔ̃ tʁɛz‿a.ni.me lə swaʁ/
notes: 'sont' (are) sounds exactly like 'son' (his or her); do not confuse them.

fr: Le policier aide les touristes perdus.
en: The police officer helps the lost tourists.
ipa: /lə pɔ.li.sje ɛd le tu.ʁist pɛʁ.dy/
notes: 'perdus' agrees in the masculine plural with 'touristes', but the final s stays silent.

fr: J'habite près de la gare centrale.
en: I live near the central train station.
ipa: /ʒa.bit pʁɛ də la ɡaʁ sɑ̃.tʁal/
notes: 'je' elides to 'j'' before the silent h of 'habite'.

fr: Les magasins ferment à dix-neuf heures.
en: The shops close at seven p.m.
ipa: /le ma.ɡa.zɛ̃ fɛʁm a diz.nœv‿œʁ/
notes: 'magasins' ends in a nasal vowel, not a separated 'ins' sound.

fr: Le marché se tient sur la place principale.
en: The market is held on the main square.
ipa: /lə maʁ.ʃe sə tjɛ̃ syʁ la plas pʁɛ̃.si.pal/
notes: The e in 'se' is a mute e that must still be written even though it is barely heard.

fr: Les touristes visitent le vieux quartier.
en: The tourists visit the old neighborhood.
ipa: /le tu.ʁist vi.zit lə vjø kaʁ.tje/
notes: The verb ending '-ent' in 'visitent' is silent.

fr: La ville est très bruyante la nuit.
en: The city is very noisy at night.
ipa: /la vil ɛ tʁɛ bʁɥi.jɑ̃t la nɥi/
notes: 'bruyante' hides a nasal 'an' sound inside its tricky spelling.

fr: Nous prenons le métro tous les jours.
en: We take the subway every day.
ipa: /nu pʁə.nɔ̃ lə me.tʁo tu le ʒuʁ/
notes: In 'tous les jours' the final s of 'tous' stays silent.

fr: Le parc est fermé après minuit.
en: The park is closed after midnight.
ipa: /lə paʁk ɛ fɛʁ.me a.pʁɛ mi.nɥi/
notes: 'est' (is) sounds just like 'et' (and); check the sentence to spell it right.

fr: Les habitants aiment leur petite ville.
en: The residents love their small town.
ipa: /lez‿a.bi.tɑ̃ ɛm lœʁ pə.tit vil/
notes: Liaison links 'les' to 'habitants' with a z sound.

fr: La circulation est difficile ce matin.
en: Traffic is difficult this morning.
ipa: /la siʁ.ky.la.sjɔ̃ ɛ di.fi.sil sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: The ending '-tion' in 'circulation' is pronounced with a nasal 'on' sound.

fr: Les immeubles sont hauts dans le centre-ville.
en: The buildings are tall downtown.
ipa: /lez‿i.mœbl sɔ̃t‿o dɑ̃ lə sɑ̃tʁ.vil/
notes: Liaison connects 'les' to 'immeubles' with a z sound.

fr: Le loyer est très cher dans cette ville.
en: Rent is very expensive in this city.
ipa: /lə lwa.je ɛ tʁɛ ʃɛʁ dɑ̃ sɛt vil/
notes: 'loyer' keeps its y even though the ending could be mistaken for '-er'.

fr: Les vélos roulent sur la piste cyclable.
en: Bicycles ride on the bike path.
ipa: /le ve.lo ʁul syʁ la pist si.klabl/
notes: The verb ending '-ent' in 'roulent' is silent.

fr: La fontaine se trouve au milieu de la place.
en: The fountain is in the middle of the square.
ipa: /la fɔ̃.tɛn sə tʁuv o mi.ljø də la plas/
notes: 'fontaine' opens with the nasal 'on' sound, spelled o-n, not a-n.

fr: Les enfants vont à l'école à pied.
en: The children go to school on foot.
ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ vɔ̃t‿a le.kɔl a pje/
notes: 'le' becomes 'l'' before the vowel sound of 'école'.

fr: La police surveille le quartier chaque nuit.
en: The police watch the neighborhood every night.
ipa: /la pɔ.lis syʁ.vɛj lə kaʁ.tje ʃak nɥi/
notes: 'surveille' uses the tricky '-eille' spelling for the sound you hear.

fr: Il y a un grand marché le samedi.
en: There is a big market on Saturdays.
ipa: /il ja œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ maʁ.ʃe lə sam.di/
notes: The final d of 'grand' is silent before a consonant.

fr: Le taxi attend devant la gare.
en: The taxi waits in front of the station.
ipa: /lə tak.si a.tɑ̃ də.vɑ̃ la ɡaʁ/
notes: The final d of 'attend' is never pronounced.

fr: Ce quartier a des rues très larges.
en: This neighborhood has very wide streets.
ipa: /sə kaʁ.tje a de ʁy tʁɛ laʁʒ/
notes: 'larges' agrees in the plural with 'rues', but the final s is silent.

fr: J'aime me promener dans les petites rues.
en: I like to walk in the small streets.
ipa: /ʒɛm mə pʁɔm.ne dɑ̃ le pə.tit ʁy/
notes: 'je' elides to 'j'' before the vowel sound of 'aime'.

fr: Le musée est ouvert tous les jours.
en: The museum is open every day.
ipa: /lə my.ze ɛt‿u.vɛʁ tu le ʒuʁ/
notes: Liaison links 'est' and 'ouvert' with a t sound.

fr: Les bus passent toutes les dix minutes.
en: Buses go by every ten minutes.
ipa: /le bys pas tut le di mi.nyt/
notes: The verb ending '-ent' in 'passent' is silent.

fr: La campagne est plus calme que la ville.
en: The countryside is calmer than the city.
ipa: /la kɑ̃.paɲ ɛ ply kalm kə la vil/
notes: 'campagne' opens with a nasal 'am' sound before the p.

fr: Les trottoirs sont pleins de monde le samedi.
en: The sidewalks are full of people on Saturdays.
ipa: /le tʁɔ.twaʁ sɔ̃ plɛ̃ də mɔ̃d lə sam.di/
notes: 'pleins' agrees in the masculine plural with 'trottoirs', though you cannot hear the s.

fr: Le centre-ville est loin de chez moi.
en: Downtown is far from my house.
ipa: /lə sɑ̃tʁ.vil ɛ lwɛ̃ də ʃe mwa/
notes: 'chez' ends in a z sound, often confused in spelling with 'ché' or 'chai'.

fr: Les gens attendent le bus sous la pluie.
en: People are waiting for the bus in the rain.
ipa: /le ʒɑ̃ a.tɑ̃d lə bys su la plɥi/
notes: 'gens' ends in a silent s, pronounced simply like 'jan'.

fr: La place principale est très jolie.
en: The main square is very pretty.
ipa: /la plas pʁɛ̃.si.pal ɛ tʁɛ ʒɔ.li/
notes: 'principale' carries a nasal 'in' sound in its first syllable.

fr: Les feux rouges sont nombreux dans cette rue.
en: There are many traffic lights on this street.
ipa: /le fø ʁuʒ sɔ̃ nɔ̃.bʁø dɑ̃ sɛt ʁy/
notes: 'nombreux' opens with a nasal 'om' sound.

fr: Le café se trouve au coin de la rue.
en: The café is on the corner of the street.
ipa: /lə ka.fe sə tʁuv o kwɛ̃ də la ʁy/
notes: The e in 'se' is a mute e that must still be written.

fr: Les habitants se plaignent souvent du bruit.
en: The residents often complain about the noise.
ipa: /lez‿a.bi.tɑ̃ sə plɛɲ su.vɑ̃ dy bʁɥi/
notes: The 'gn' in 'plaignent' makes a single nasal-consonant sound, easy to misspell.

fr: La ville grandit un peu plus chaque année.
en: The city grows a little more every year.
ipa: /la vil ɡʁɑ̃.di œ̃ pø ply ʃak a.ne/
notes: The final t of 'grandit' is silent.

fr: Les parcs sont pleins le week-end.
en: The parks are full on the weekend.
ipa: /le paʁk sɔ̃ plɛ̃ lə wi.kɛnd/
notes: 'pleins' takes a silent final s to agree with 'parcs'.

fr: Le commissariat est ouvert vingt-quatre heures sur vingt-quatre.
en: The police station is open twenty-four hours a day.
ipa: /lə kɔ.mi.sa.ʁja ɛt‿u.vɛʁ vɛ̃t.katʁ‿œʁ syʁ vɛ̃t.katʁ/
notes: 'vingt' ends in a nasal vowel; its final consonants are not pronounced.

fr: Les employés nettoient les rues tôt le matin.
en: Workers clean the streets early in the morning.
ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃.plwa.je nɛ.twa le ʁy to lə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'employés' opens with a nasal 'em' sound spelled e-m.

fr: J'aime la vie tranquille de mon quartier.
en: I like the quiet life of my neighborhood.
ipa: /ʒɛm la vi tʁɑ̃.kil də mɔ̃ kaʁ.tje/
notes: 'tranquille' opens with a nasal 'an' sound.

fr: Le tramway traverse toute la ville en dix minutes.
en: The tram crosses the whole city in ten minutes.
ipa: /lə tʁam.wɛ tʁa.vɛʁs tut la vil ɑ̃ di mi.nyt/
notes: 'tramway' keeps its English w spelling, pronounced like an English w.

fr: Chaque année, les citoyens votent pour le maire.
en: Every year, the citizens vote for the mayor.
ipa: /ʃak a.ne le si.twa.jɛ̃ vɔt puʁ lə mɛʁ/
notes: 'maire' (mayor) sounds exactly like 'mère' (mother) and 'mer' (sea).

fr: La ville organise un marché de Noël en décembre.
en: The city organizes a Christmas market in December.
ipa: /la vil ɔʁ.ɡa.niz œ̃ maʁ.ʃe də nɔ.ɛl ɑ̃ de.sɑ̃bʁ/
notes: 'décembre' hides a nasal 'em' sound spelled with m before b.

fr: Les touristes prennent des photos partout.
en: The tourists take photos everywhere.
ipa: /le tu.ʁist pʁɛn de fɔ.to paʁ.tu/
notes: The verb ending '-ent' in 'prennent' is silent, not pronounced.

fr: Le pont relie les deux quartiers de la ville.
en: The bridge links the two neighborhoods of the city.
ipa: /lə pɔ̃ ʁə.li le dø kaʁ.tje də la vil/
notes: The final t of 'pont' is silent.

fr: Les trains partent de la gare du nord.
en: The trains leave from the north station.
ipa: /le tʁɛ̃ paʁt də la ɡaʁ dy nɔʁ/
notes: 'trains' ends in a nasal vowel, with a silent final s.

fr: La rue principale est fermée aujourd'hui.
en: The main street is closed today.
ipa: /la ʁy pʁɛ̃.si.pal ɛ fɛʁ.me o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: 'aujourd'hui' contains a fixed elision that must be written with an apostrophe.

fr: Près de la fontaine, les enfants aiment jouer.
en: Near the fountain, the children like to play.
ipa: /pʁɛ də la fɔ̃.tɛn lez‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ɛm ʒwe/
notes: The mute e's in 'de la' are barely heard but always written.

fr: Le quartier est calme le dimanche matin.
en: The neighborhood is quiet on Sunday morning.
ipa: /lə kaʁ.tje ɛ kalm lə di.mɑ̃ʃ ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'dimanche' carries a nasal 'an' sound in its second syllable.

fr: Le silence règne dans le parc le matin.
en: Silence reigns in the park in the morning.
ipa: /lə si.lɑ̃s ʁɛɲ dɑ̃ lə paʁk lə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'règne' needs a grave accent on the first e to keep the right sound.

fr: La ville compte deux cent mille habitants.
en: The city has two hundred thousand inhabitants.
ipa: /la vil kɔ̃t dø sɑ̃ mil a.bi.tɑ̃/
notes: 'cent' (hundred) sounds identical to 'sans' (without) and 'sang' (blood).

fr: Chaque année, la mairie décore les rues pour les fêtes.
en: Every year, the town hall decorates the streets for the holidays.
ipa: /ʃak a.ne la mɛ.ʁi de.kɔʁ le ʁy puʁ le fɛt/
notes: The verb 'décore' is easily confused in spelling with the noun 'décor'.

fr: Le musée municipal ouvre gratuitement le premier dimanche.
en: The municipal museum opens free of charge on the first Sunday.
ipa: /lə my.ze my.ni.si.pal uvʁ ɡʁa.tɥit.mɑ̃ lə pʁə.mje di.mɑ̃ʃ/
notes: 'gratuitement' keeps its tricky 'ui' spelling even though it is said quickly.

fr: Les magasins du centre-ville ferment tôt le lundi.
en: The downtown shops close early on Mondays.
ipa: /le ma.ɡa.zɛ̃ dy sɑ̃tʁ.vil fɛʁm to lə lœ̃.di/
notes: 'lundi' opens with the nasal vowel 'un', distinct from 'on' or 'in'.

fr: Je suis allé à la mairie ce matin.
en: I went to the town hall this morning.
ipa: /ʒə sɥi a.le a la mɛ.ʁi sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: With être, the past participle 'allé' agrees with the subject; a woman would have to write 'allée'.

fr: Elle est allée à la bibliothèque hier.
en: She went to the library yesterday.
ipa: /ɛl ɛt‿a.le a la bi.bli.jɔ.tɛk jɛʁ/
notes: 'allée' takes a silent extra e to agree with the feminine subject 'elle'.

fr: Nous avons visité le musée samedi dernier.
en: We visited the museum last Saturday.
ipa: /nuz‿a.vɔ̃ vi.zi.te lə my.ze sam.di dɛʁ.nje/
notes: With avoir and no object before the verb, 'visité' stays invariable, unlike the infinitive 'visiter' which sounds the same.

fr: Ils sont arrivés en retard à la gare.
en: They arrived late at the station.
ipa: /il sɔ̃t‿a.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ a la ɡaʁ/
notes: 'arrivés' takes a silent plural s to agree with the masculine plural subject 'ils'.

fr: Elles sont parties tôt ce matin.
en: They (women) left early this morning.
ipa: /ɛl sɔ̃ paʁ.ti to sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'parties' takes a silent -es to agree with the feminine plural subject 'elles'.

fr: J'ai pris le bus pour aller au travail.
en: I took the bus to go to work.
ipa: /ʒe pʁi lə bys puʁ a.le o tʁa.vaj/
notes: The irregular past participle 'pris' ends in a silent s.

fr: Le maire a inauguré le nouveau parc hier.
en: The mayor inaugurated the new park yesterday.
ipa: /lə mɛʁ a i.no.ɡy.ʁe lə nu.vo paʁk jɛʁ/
notes: 'inauguré' and the infinitive 'inaugurer' sound identical, only the ending spelling differs.

fr: La mairie que j'ai visitée est très ancienne.
en: The town hall that I visited is very old.
ipa: /la mɛ.ʁi kə ʒe vi.zi.te ɛ tʁɛz‿ɑ̃.sjɛn/
notes: Because 'que' refers back to the feminine 'la mairie' placed before the verb, 'visitée' must agree and take a silent e.

fr: Les touristes ont pris le bus pour visiter la vieille ville.
en: The tourists took the bus to visit the old town.
ipa: /le tu.ʁist ɔ̃ pʁi lə bys puʁ vi.zi.te la vjɛj vil/
notes: 'ont' (have) must not be confused with 'on' (one), even though they sound identical.

fr: On a construit un nouveau pont cette année.
en: They built a new bridge this year.
ipa: /ɔ̃ a kɔ̃s.tʁɥi œ̃ nu.vo pɔ̃ sɛt a.ne/
notes: 'on' always takes a singular verb like 'a', never the plural 'ont'.

fr: Les rues ont été refaites après les travaux.
en: The streets were redone after the roadworks.
ipa: /le ʁy ɔ̃t‿e.te ʁə.fɛt a.pʁɛ le tʁa.vo/
notes: 'refaites' agrees in the feminine plural with 'les rues', though the ending is not heard.

fr: Nous allons visiter le nouveau quartier demain.
en: We are going to visit the new neighborhood tomorrow.
ipa: /nuz‿a.lɔ̃ vi.zi.te lə nu.vo kaʁ.tje də.mɛ̃/
notes: After 'aller', the next verb stays an infinitive ('visiter'), not the past participle 'visité', though they sound alike.

fr: Je vais prendre le métro pour aller au centre-ville.
en: I am going to take the subway to go downtown.
ipa: /ʒə vɛ pʁɑ̃dʁ lə me.tʁo puʁ a.le o sɑ̃tʁ.vil/
notes: 'aller' plus the infinitive 'prendre' signals the near future; do not write a past participle here.

fr: Il a décidé d'aller à la mairie cet après-midi.
en: He decided to go to the town hall this afternoon.
ipa: /il a de.si.de da.le a la mɛ.ʁi sɛt‿a.pʁɛ.mi.di/
notes: 'a' (has) and 'à' (to) sound exactly the same; the accent is the only difference.

fr: Elle va habiter dans le centre-ville l'année prochaine.
en: She is going to live downtown next year.
ipa: /ɛl va a.bi.te dɑ̃ lə sɑ̃tʁ.vil la.ne pʁɔ.ʃɛn/
notes: 'va habiter' uses the infinitive after 'aller', not a past form, even though the endings can sound similar.

fr: Nous avons marché jusqu'à la place principale.
en: We walked to the main square.
ipa: /nuz‿a.vɔ̃ maʁ.ʃe ʒys.ka la plas pʁɛ̃.si.pal/
notes: 'marché' (walked) and 'marcher' (to walk) are pronounced the same; check whether the action is finished.

fr: As-tu vu le nouveau musée du quartier ?
en: Have you seen the new neighborhood museum?
ipa: /a ty vy lə nu.vo my.ze dy kaʁ.tje/
notes: The participle 'vu' stays invariable here because its direct object 'le musée' comes after the verb, not before.

fr: Où se trouve la station de métro la plus proche ?
en: Where is the nearest subway station?
ipa: /u sə tʁuv la sta.sjɔ̃ də me.tʁo la ply pʁɔʃ/
notes: 'où' (where) keeps its grave accent, unlike the conjunction 'ou' (or).

fr: Je ne sais pas où se trouve la mairie.
en: I don't know where the town hall is.
ipa: /ʒə nə sɛ pa u sə tʁuv la mɛ.ʁi/
notes: 'où' takes a grave accent because it asks about a location, unlike 'ou' meaning 'or'.

fr: Il a demandé où était le commissariat.
en: He asked where the police station was.
ipa: /il a də.mɑ̃.de u e.tɛ lə kɔ.mi.sa.ʁja/
notes: 'où' keeps its accent even inside an indirect question.

fr: Ou vous prenez le bus, ou vous marchez jusqu'au centre.
en: Either you take the bus, or you walk to the center.
ipa: /u vu pʁə.ne lə bys u vu maʁ.ʃe ʒys.ko sɑ̃tʁ/
notes: This 'ou' (or) has no accent, unlike the location word 'où'.

fr: Le samedi, on va au marché ou on reste à la maison.
en: On Saturdays, we go to the market or we stay home.
ipa: /lə sam.di ɔ̃ va o maʁ.ʃe u ɔ̃ ʁɛst a la mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: 'ou' (or) here has no accent, unlike 'où' which marks a place.

fr: Les enfants sont allés au parc après l'école.
en: The children went to the park after school.
ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ sɔ̃t‿a.le o paʁk a.pʁɛ le.kɔl/
notes: 'allés' agrees in the masculine plural with 'les enfants', but the s is silent.

fr: La police a arrêté deux hommes en ville hier soir.
en: The police arrested two men in the city last night.
ipa: /la pɔ.lis a a.ʁɛ.te døz‿ɔm ɑ̃ vil jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: With avoir and the object 'deux hommes' after the verb, 'arrêté' stays in its base form.

fr: Les touristes que j'ai rencontrés hier venaient de Chine.
en: The tourists I met yesterday were from China.
ipa: /le tu.ʁist kə ʒe ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe jɛʁ və.nɛ də ʃin/
notes: 'que' refers back to 'les touristes' placed before the verb, so 'rencontrés' must agree in the masculine plural.

fr: Nous avons décidé de déménager en ville l'an prochain.
en: We decided to move to the city next year.
ipa: /nuz‿a.vɔ̃ de.si.de də de.me.na.ʒe ɑ̃ vil lɑ̃ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃/
notes: 'décidé' and 'déménager' both end in the same sound though one is a past participle and the other an infinitive.

fr: Ils ont emménagé dans un appartement du centre-ville.
en: They moved into an apartment downtown.
ipa: /ilz‿ɔ̃t‿ɑ̃.me.na.ʒe dɑ̃z‿œ̃n‿a.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃ dy sɑ̃tʁ.vil/
notes: 'ont' (have) is easily confused in spelling with 'on' (one), though they sound identical.

fr: La circulation a beaucoup augmenté depuis dix ans.
en: Traffic has increased a lot in the last ten years.
ipa: /la siʁ.ky.la.sjɔ̃ a bo.ku oɡ.mɑ̃.te də.pɥi diz‿ɑ̃/
notes: 'augmenté' stays invariable with avoir since there is no direct object before the verb.

fr: On a trouvé un stationnement gratuit près de la mairie.
en: We found free parking near the town hall.
ipa: /ɔ̃ a tʁu.ve œ̃ sta.sjɔn.mɑ̃ ɡʁa.tɥi pʁɛ də la mɛ.ʁi/
notes: 'on' is always followed by a singular verb like 'a', never the plural 'ont'.

fr: Mes parents ont grandi dans cette ville.
en: My parents grew up in this city.
ipa: /me pa.ʁɑ̃ ɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃.di dɑ̃ sɛt vil/
notes: 'ont' (have) is easily confused in spelling with 'on' (one), though pronounced identically.

fr: Le loyer a augmenté à cause du manque de logements.
en: Rent has increased because of the housing shortage.
ipa: /lə lwa.je a oɡ.mɑ̃.te a koz dy mɑ̃k də lɔ.ʒə.mɑ̃/
notes: 'logements' ends in a nasal sound spelled '-ements', not pronounced letter by letter.

fr: Beaucoup de gens ont quitté la campagne pour la ville.
en: Many people have left the countryside for the city.
ipa: /bo.ku də ʒɑ̃ ɔ̃ ki.te la kɑ̃.paɲ puʁ la vil/
notes: 'quitté' stays invariable with avoir because 'la campagne' comes after the verb, not before.

fr: Cette ville, je l'ai visitée plusieurs fois.
en: This city, I have visited it several times.
ipa: /sɛt vil ʒə le vi.zi.te ply.zjœʁ fwa/
notes: 'l'' referring to the feminine 'cette ville' comes before 'ai visitée', so the past participle must agree and take a silent e.

fr: Le nouveau maire va organiser un grand festival en juillet.
en: The new mayor is going to organize a big festival in July.
ipa: /lə nu.vo mɛʁ va ɔʁ.ɡa.ni.ze œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ fɛs.ti.val ɑ̃ ʒɥi.jɛ/
notes: 'organiser' stays an infinitive after 'va', not the participle 'organisé', although they sound alike.

fr: J'ai entendu dire que le musée va fermer bientôt.
en: I heard that the museum is going to close soon.
ipa: /ʒe ɑ̃.tɑ̃.dy diʁ kə lə my.ze va fɛʁ.me bjɛ̃.to/
notes: 'fermer' after 'va' must keep its infinitive -er ending, not become 'fermé'.

fr: La mairie a annoncé que les impôts vont augmenter.
en: The town hall announced that taxes are going to increase.
ipa: /la mɛ.ʁi a a.nɔ̃.se kə lez‿ɛ̃.po vɔ̃t‿oɡ.mɑ̃.te/
notes: 'augmenter' keeps its infinitive -er ending after 'vont', unlike the past participle 'augmenté'.

fr: Ils vont bientôt inaugurer la nouvelle bibliothèque municipale.
en: They are soon going to inaugurate the new municipal library.
ipa: /il vɔ̃ bjɛ̃.to i.no.ɡy.ʁe la nu.vɛl bi.bli.jɔ.tɛk my.ni.si.pal/
notes: 'inaugurer' stays an infinitive after 'vont', not 'inauguré', even though the sounds match.

fr: Nous avons enfin trouvé un appartement calme en ville.
en: We finally found a quiet apartment in the city.
ipa: /nuz‿a.vɔ̃z‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ tʁu.ve œ̃n‿a.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃ kalm ɑ̃ vil/
notes: 'trouvé' stays invariable with avoir since 'un appartement' follows the verb rather than preceding it.
